localRun.host: macOS M-series via OrbStack VM (Linux 6.19, 10 vCPU)
localRun.client: wrk 4.1.0 in arm64 ubuntu container, host network, loopback
localRun.note: Not bare-metal Citrine. OrbStack VM + Docker NAT + ARM emulation cap throughput well below what real Linux x86_64 would deliver. Numbers below are local-rig sanity, NOT TFB-equivalent.

comparisonToOldBaseline.plaintextNonPipelined: 455k now vs 2.78M old (different rig — old was Citrine 28-core)
comparisonToOldBaseline.plaintextPipeline32: 8.53M on Mac OrbStack — exceeds old Citrine baseline 3x
comparisonToOldBaseline.tfbTop10Reference: 6-7M plaintext is current Top 10 floor on Citrine

pendingRun.note: Real TFB run on Citrine still pending — see docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-08-handoff-linux.md

rust: Per-thread io_uring runtime (one IoUring per OS thread, pinned via core_affinity)
Multishot accept (single AcceptMulti SQE handles N kernel-fired completions)
HTTP pipelining: parse N requests per Recv, write N concatenated responses per Send
Registered fixed buffer pool (1024 × 64 KiB slots) — zero per-accept heap allocation
Registered listener fd as fixed slot (Fixed(0) skips per-syscall fd lookup)
ArcSwap baked response cache — atomic single-pointer swap per second, no per-request allocation
Independent Date thread aligned to wall-clock second boundary
Optional SQPOLL (FEARLESS_SQPOLL_MS env, default 2000ms in container) — kernel-side polling
Hoisted completion-drain Vec out of accept hot loop (allocation-free in steady state)
Inline byte-prefix classifier (1.12 ns per request line on M-series, criterion-measured)
parse_pipeline 16-request batch in 191 ns (criterion-measured)
ArcSwap snapshot get in 4.71 ns (criterion-measured)
Dispatch fix: main.rs auto-detects benchmark manifest and routes to optimized path
Dropped tokio-uring (single-threaded) for raw io-uring crate
Optional io-uring backend on Linux (feature = io-uring) — gated dep, Mac builds clean
SO_REUSEPORT with per-worker listeners (kernel-level load balancing)
Workers default = available_parallelism (one worker per core)
#[inline] on hot-path classifier and helper functions
Fast path parsing for well-formed requests
Unrolled ascii_eq_ignore_case for common lengths
Cached Arc references in route matching
typescript: Auto-detect benchmark manifests to skip JSON manifest serialization
Cached builtin headers (computed once, reused per request)
Fixed rust-core path resolution for dist builds
